sources.title: OME-NGFF 0.4 Final Community Group Report
sources.pin: 0.4 edition as published at the edition URL; capture SHA-256 ca4780a33f9561cfd2d983651fdcc745dce0d6089f5cf775744a54e8394a5269 (page identifies itself as the 0.4 release and records a 0.4.1 transitional metadata revision)
sources.applicability: Authoritative specification for the proposed local OME-Zarr boundary: axis names/types/order, 2–5 dimensions, scale/translation metadata, channel display metadata, and integer image-label masks. It does not specify our SQLite project, full vector annotation schema, application performance, arbitrary affine transforms, or importer conformance.

sources.title: OME-TIFF Specification, OME Data Model and File Formats 6.2.2
sources.applicability: Defines how OME-XML, TIFF IFDs, plane dimension order, explicit mapping, and multi-file UUID references relate. It does not establish a reader's behavior on every producer's malformed or ambiguous metadata.

capture.candidate_inspected: Specification text included in initial response capture, including DimensionOrder, TiffData and multi-file sections.

sources.title: tifffile README / implementation notes
sources.pin: Git tag v2024.9.20; README declares version 2024.9.20. Requirements list Zarr 2.18.3, imagecodecs 2024.6.1, and NumPy 2.1.1 among the tested requirements.
locators: Use Zarr to read parts of tiled pyramidal images
Load base layer as Dask array
sources.applicability: Implementation precedent and candidate reader spike pin. Documents selected Zarr-backed reads, dtype/format boundaries, compression dependency, and exclusions including multi-file pyramidal OME-TIFF. Examples and declared tested dependencies do not prove target-machine performance or application correctness.

capture.candidate_inspected: Complete README text supplied in response.

sources.pin: Git tag v0.5.6; exact source path above; capture SHA-256 a2cbf1a542beff08d29e7118b62cc6df3f82c8e928a40ffb861d6ea9076faed1
locators: Shapes class docstring: data dimensions and list of supported geometries

sources.applicability: Evidence for the proposed annotation interaction prototype: vector shape geometry, point-free shape operations, attributes, transforms, and interactive modes are present in this version's implementation. Not evidence of durable project persistence, our undo/redo contract, correct arbitrary image calibration, or out-of-core behavior beyond the documented cache parameter.

sources.title: SQLite Atomic Commit In SQLite
sources.pin: Mutable official documentation page captured 2026-10-06; pinned evidence is response body SHA-256 5a5be7b660217c9408c8a81eaf2faa2d08832ed3790f895a0a713916ad856ea1; not a release-tagged SQLite library source
locators: Introduction: atomic transaction property and rollback-mode scope
sources.applicability: Supports the transactional-save/recovery design and its assumptions. It is not a guarantee about SMB/NFS or this application's chosen OS/filesystem; WAL uses a different mechanism and is not the mode relied on by this proposal.

capture.candidate_inspected: Atomic commit introduction, scope and assumptions, rollback flow through single-file commit, and failure caveats.
